Iran raised the initiative at the UN General Assembly in New York, saying it had been transmitted to the US via Qatari mediators and that it could reopen the strategic waterway and put an end to hostilities in the region within seven days. The US has imposed an economic blockade on Iran to pressure it to lift its blockade of Hormuz, which has drastically reduced shipping through the strait, even though Trump again asserted that the US had control of the waterway. The Wall Street Journal first reported that Trump had rejected the Iranian proposal, citing unnamed US officials. It said Trump was privately sceptical that Iran would meet his demands and had told his staff that he sees a renewed bombing campaign as likely after the November US midterm elections to Congress. (SEPTEMBER 26): President Trump has rejected Iran’s seven-day proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. “I rejected their deal. They want to make a deal where they open the strait immediately because they’re losing so badly,” Trump told reporters as he departed the White House. “You know why they’re dying? Because they have no money coming in because they get their money from the Hormuz Strait.” Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi had said Friday that Tehran submitted a “concrete seven-day plan” through Qatari mediators — one he described as asking for nothing beyond what was already agreed to in June’s Memorandum of Understanding, which collapsed within days of being signed. Trump said he remains open to negotiating in general: “They want to make a deal and I think that’s fine. I’d like to make a deal, too. But that deal would not be acceptable.”
